questions.question: Due to an increase of 20 percent in the price of rice, the consumer decreases his consumption by 5 percent. What is the percentage change in total expenditure?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **net percentage change** formula: Net % = a + b + (ab / 100).

Here, a = +20 (**increase**) and b = −5 (**decrease**).

Net Change = 20 − 5 + [20 × (−5) / 100]

Net Change = 15 − (100 / 100) = 15 − 1 = 14%.

Since the result is positive, it is a 14% **increase** in expenditure.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Price increase** = 20%

**Consumption decrease** = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Total Expenditure = **Price** × **Consumption**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c4f99a69115ed996a6792bc2eca8aed5880a5cbfca4bd3d681c6aa3e4465c67f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original Price = 100 and original Consumption = 100

⇒ Original Expenditure = 100 × 100 = 10000

⇒ New Price = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120

⇒ New Consumption = 100 − 5% of 100 = 95

⇒ New Expenditure = 120 × 95 = 11400

⇒ Change in Expenditure = 11400 − 10000 = 1400

⇒ Percentage Change = (1400 / 10000) × 100

⇒ Percentage Change = 14%

**∴ The correct answer is 14 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net effective change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

Price-Consumption-Expenditure Relation

If expenditure is kept constant, price and consumption are inversely proportional (Price ∝ 1 / Consumption).

Ratio Method

Price ratio = 100:120 = 5:6. Consumption ratio = 100:95 = 20:19. Expenditure ratio = (5×20):(6×19) = 100:114.</p

questions.question: If a + b = 3 and ab = 2, then what is the value of 2a³ + 2b³?
questions.solution:
**Given**

a + b = 3

ab = 2

**Concept:**

This is the formula to simplify cubic expressions: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²)

**Solution:**

2a³ + 2b³ = 2(a³ + b³)

2(a + b)(a² - ab + b²) (Substituting from given)

2(3)(a² - 2 + b²) (as a + b = 3 and ab = 2)

2(3)(a² + b² - 2) (as a² + b² = (a + b)² - 2ab = 9 - 4 = 5)

2(3)(5 - 2) = 2(3)(3) = 18

**fore, the value of 2a³ + 2b³ is 18.**

questions.question: In a cyclic quadrilateral A B C D, ∠A is opposite to ∠C. If ∠A = 110 degree, then what is the value of ∠C?
questions.solution:
**Given**

In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary (i.e., they add up to 180°).

**Solution:**

∠C = 180° - 110° = 70°

questions.question: If P+(1)/(P)=5, then what is the value of P³+(1)/(P³)?
questions.solution:
**Given**

P + 1/P = 5

**Concept:**

Cubic equation formula from quadratic equation: If P + 1/P = n, then P³ + 1/P³ = n³ - 3n

**Solution:**

P³ + 1/P³ = 5³ - 3×5

P³ + 1/P³ = 125 - 15 = 110

**The value of P³ + 1/P³ is 110.**

questions.question: If K+(1)/(K)=-3, then what is the value of [2((K⁶+1)/(K³))]+((K⁴+1)/(K²))?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If **K + 1/K = a**, then **K² + 1/K² = a² − 2** and **K³ + 1/K³ = a³ − 3a**.

Given **K + 1/K = −3**, so **a = −3**.

K² + 1/K² = (−3)² − 2 = 7.

K³ + 1/K³ = (−3)³ − 3(−3) = −27 + 9 = −18.

Required Expression = 2(K³ + 1/K³) + (K² + 1/K²) = 2(−18) + 7 = −29.

**∴ The correct answer is −29.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** K + 1/K = −3

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ Square the given equation: (K + 1/K)² = (−3)²

⇒ K² + 1/K² + 2 = 9

⇒ **K² + 1/K² = 7**

⇒ Cube the given equation: (K + 1/K)³ = (−3)³

⇒ K³ + 1/K³ + 3(K)(1/K)(K + 1/K) = −27

⇒ K³ + 1/K³ + 3(−3) = −27

⇒ **K³ + 1/K³ = −18**

⇒ [2((K⁶ + 1) / K³)] + ((K⁴ + 1) / K²) = 2(K³ + 1/K³) + (K² + 1/K²)

⇒ Value = 2(−18) + 7

⇒ Value = −36 + 7 = −29

**∴ The correct answer is −29.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Power 2

For any variable x, x² + 1/x² = (x + 1/x)² − 2.

Algebraic Identity for Power 3

For any variable x, x³ + 1/x³ = (x + 1/x)³ − 3(x + 1/x).

Algebraic Identity for Power 4

x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = (x² + 1/x²)² − 2. This can be derived by squaring the power 2 identity.</p

questions.question: Selling price of a watch is Rs. 1056 and profit percentage is 10 percent. If selling price is Rs. 800 , then what will be the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The reasoning involves determining the **Cost Price** using the given **Selling Price** and **Profit Percentage**, followed by calculating the **Loss Percentage** for the new **Selling Price**.

Initial SP = 110% of CP = 1056.

CP = 1056 ÷ 1.1 = 960.

New SP = 800.

Loss = 960 − 800 = 160.

Loss% = (160 ÷ 960) × 100 = 16.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67 percent.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given → SP₁ = 1056, Profit₁ = 10%, SP₂ = 800.
Formulas: CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + P%) | Loss% = (CP − SP) ÷ CP × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/55ee2239de95ace74475bc57b62a2b035ddf28aeb0b539edc20bb2f69cc2fc14.png] 
⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 1056 × 100 ÷ 110 = 960.
⇒ **Loss** = 960 − 800 = 160.
⇒ **Loss Percentage** = (160 ÷ 960) × 100.
⇒ **Loss Percentage** = 100 ÷ 6 = 16.666...% ≈ 16.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67 percent.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cost Price and Selling Price

The **Cost Price** is the base for calculating **Profit** or **Loss** unless specified otherwise. CP = SP − Profit or CP = SP + Loss.

Loss Percentage

**Loss%** = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. It indicates the amount of value lost relative to the original investment.</p

questions.question: What is the value of frac{3 operatorname{cosec} 42circ}{sec 48circ}-frac{5 cos 32circ}{sin 58circ}
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify **complementary angles**: 42° + 48° = 90° and 32° + 58° = 90°.

Using the property: If **A + B = 90°**, then **csc A / sec B = 1** and **cos A / sin B = 1**.

Expression = 3(1) − 5(1)

Expression = 3 − 5 = −2.

**∴ The correct answer is -2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (3 csc 42° / sec 48°) − (5 cos 32° / sin 58°)

**Formula Used:** csc θ = sec(90° − θ) and cos θ = sin(90° − θ)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35fba40671bdd4aef535d575a0fde5404dfd08811b008df290d5d93d76829d3f.png] 

⇒ csc 42° = sec(90° − 42°) = sec 48°

⇒ cos 32° = sin(90° − 32°) = sin 58°

⇒ Expression = [3 × sec 48° / sec 48°] − [5 × sin 58° / sin 58°]

⇒ Expression = 3(1) − 5(1)

⇒ Expression = 3 − 5 = −2

**∴ The correct answer is -2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios of Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90°. Basic identities include sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and tan(90° − θ) = cot θ.

Secant and Cosecant Relationship

The secant of an angle is equal to the cosecant of its complement: sec θ = csc(90° − θ).

Quotient Property for Complementary Angles

If A + B = 90°, then sin A / cos B = 1, tan A / cot B = 1, and sec A / csc B = 1.</p

The pie chart given below show the runs scored by 5 batsmen in a cricket match. Total runs scored by these batsmen are 300 . Runs scored by a batsman is shown as a percentage of runs scored by all these five batsmen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f852125256623d0f1d9b33d469a865e1c209ef1945d452b014a6d03c92a93f1.png] 

What is the average runs scored in F, I and J?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Percentage of runs for F = 18%, I = 24%, J = 6%; Total runs = 300

**Concept:**

The average of a quantity is the sum of all quantities divided by the number of quantities.

**Solution:**

Calculate runs for F, I, and J: F = 18% of 300 = 54, I = 24% of 300 = 72, J = 6% of 300 = 18

Calculate average: (F + I + J)/3 = (54 + 72 + 18)/3 = 48

**Hence, the average runs scored in F, I and J is 48**

questions.question: The length of a cuboid is thrice of its breadth and the height of cuboid is twice of its breadth. If the breadth of the cuboid is 6 cm. then what is the total surface area of cuboid?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of dimensions **Length** (L) : **Breadth** (B) : **Height** (H) = 3 : 1 : 2

Given **Breadth** (1 unit) = 6 cm ⇒ **Length** = 18 cm and **Height** = 12 cm.

**Total Surface Area** = 2 × (LB + BH + LH)

Area = 2 × (18 × 6 + 6 × 12 + 12 × 18) = 2 × (108 + 72 + 216) = 2 × 396 = 792 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 792 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Breadth** (b) of the cuboid = 6 cm

**Length** (l) = 3 × **Breadth** = 3 × 6 = 18 cm

**Height** (h) = 2 × **Breadth** = 2 × 6 = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Total Surface Area (TSA)** of a cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e30ad160696db28a62d47e5195d843d86c79c1116d792fa78792aaf8f170c9df.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **TSA** = 2 × (18 × 6 + 6 × 12 + 12 × 18)

⇒ **TSA** = 2 × (108 + 72 + 216)

⇒ **TSA** = 2 × 396

⇒ **TSA** = 792 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 792 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The space occupied by the cuboid is calculated as Volume = Length × Breadth × Height.

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

The area of the four vertical faces (excluding top and bottom) is LSA = 2 × Height × (Length + Breadth).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is the diagonal, given by √(l² + b² + h²).</p

questions.question: Two circles having equal radius intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of the other. Length of the common chord is 24 cm, then what will be the diameter of each circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two **equal circles** passing through each other's centers, the **common chord** length is given by: L = √3 × r.

⇒ 24 = √3 × r

⇒ r = 24 / √3 = 8√3 cm

⇒ **Diameter** of the circle (d) = 2 × r = 2 × 8√3

⇒ d = 16√3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 16√3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of both circles = r cm

Length of the **common chord** (AB) = 24 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a triangle, the line joining the centers of two circles is the perpendicular bisector of their common chord. **Pythagoras theorem**: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a0962bbae1ca5d07b2e12ad95b5ceb6cc942b7445f6314d92017778bc1447879.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let O₁ and O₂ be the centers of the two circles.

⇒ O₁O₂ = Radius (r) (since each passes through the other's center)

⇒ In ΔO₁MA, where M is the midpoint of AB and O₁O₂:

⇒ AM = AB ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm

⇒ O₁M = O₁O₂ ÷ 2 = r ÷ 2

⇒ O₁A = Radius = r

⇒ Using Pythagoras theorem: O₁A² = O₁M² + AM²

⇒ r² = (r/2)² + 12²

⇒ r² − r²/4 = 144

⇒ 3r² / 4 = 144

⇒ r² = (144 × 4) ÷ 3 = 48 × 4 = 192

⇒ r = √192 = 8√3 cm

⇒ Diameter = 2 × r = 2 × 8√3 = 16√3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 16√3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Common Chord Property

The line joining the centers of two intersecting circles is the **perpendicular bisector** of their common chord.

Intersecting Equal Circles

When two equal circles pass through each other's **centers**, they form two **equilateral triangles** with the intersection points and the centers, all sides being equal to the radius r.

Common Chord Length Formula

If two circles of radii r₁ and r₂ have centers at distance d, the length of the common chord is 2 × √[r₁² − ((r₁² − r₂² + d²) ÷ 2d)²].</p

questions.question: If A = a cosec θ + b cot θ and B = a cot θ + b cosec θ, then what is the value of A² - B²?
questions.solution:
**Given**

A = a cosec θ + b cot θ

B = a cot θ + b cosec θ

**Concept:**

A trigonometric identity can be used here: cosec² θ - cot² θ = 1

**Solution:**

Substitute the given values into the formula: A² - B² = (a² - b²)(cosec² θ - cot² θ) = (a² - b²) × 1 = a² - b²

**Hence, the value of A² - B² is a² - b².**

questions.question: P, Q and R can complete a work alone in 12,15 and 20 days respectively. They started the work together. P left the work 8 days before the work was completed and Q left the work 5 days after P had left. R completed the remaining work alone. How many days will be required to complete the whole work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P can complete the work in 12 days.

Q can complete the work in 15 days.

R can complete the work in 20 days.

P left the work 8 days before it was completed.

Q left the work 5 days after P had left.

R completed the remaining work alone.

**Concept:**

The total work done by individuals working together is equal to the sum of their individual work done in the same time.

**Solution:**

Total work = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60

Efficiency of P = 60/12 = 5

Efficiency of Q = 60/15 = 4

Efficiency of R = 60/20 = 3

Let the total work done in t days.

According to question,

⇒ 5(t - 8) + 4(t - 3) + 3t = 60

⇒ 5t - 40 + 4t - 12 + 3t = 60

⇒ 12t = 112

⇒ t = 112/12 = 28/3 days

**∴ 28/3 days will be required to complete the whole work.**

questions.question: A bus starts from a bus stand after every 50 minutes in the same direction. Mohit is walking in opposite direction with a speed of 50 km/hr. If Mohit meets each bus in 10 minutes, then what is the speed of bus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The distance covered by the bus in (50 − 10) = 40 minutes is equal to the distance covered by Mohit in 10 minutes.

Since the distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time.

Ratio of Time (Bus : Mohit) = 40 : 10 = 4 : 1

Ratio of Speed (Bus : Mohit) = 1 : 4

Mohit's speed = 4 units ⇒ 50 km/hr, so Bus's speed = 1 unit ⇒ 50 ÷ 4 = 12.5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Bus frequency time = 50 mins

Mohit's meeting time with each bus = 10 mins

Mohit's speed = 50 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

 
• Next Bus Mohit Meet in 10 mins 
 
 Bus travels for 10 mins Mohit travels for 10 mins 
• 
• 
• Initial Gap = Bus Speed × 50 mins 
 
 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the bus be V km/hr.

⇒ Distance between two consecutive buses = V × (50/60) km

⇒ Relative speed of Bus and Mohit = (V + 50) km/hr

⇒ Time taken to meet = 10/60 hours

We know, Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ 10/60 = [V × (50/60)] ÷ (V + 50)

⇒ 1/6 = (5V/6) ÷ (V + 50)

⇒ (V + 50) / 6 = 5V / 6

⇒ V + 50 = 5V

⇒ 4V = 50

⇒ V = 12.5

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies are moving in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Distance in Periodic Events

If a bus or train departs periodically after every T interval, the constant distance maintained between any two consecutive vehicles on the route is D = Speed × T.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 150 percent of the cost price. If 20 percent discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Marked price is 150% of the cost price

Discount given is 20%

**Concept:**

Profit percentage is calculated as (Selling price - Cost price)/Cost price × 100%

**Solution:**

Selling price after discount = 150% - 20% of 150% = 150% - 30% = 120%

Profit percentage = (Selling price - Cost price)/Cost price × 100% = (120% - 100%)/100% × 100% = 20%

**Therefore, the profit percentage is 20%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**MP/CP = (100 + profit%)/(100 - loss%)

150/100 = (100 + p)/80 ⇒ P = 120 -100 = 20%

questions.question: An amount of Rs.12,029 is divided among P, Q and R such that P's share is 5 times Q's share and R's share is one-third of P's share. What is the share of R?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Total amount = Rs. 12,029

P's share = 5Q

R's share = P/3

**Concept:**

The total amount is the sum of the shares of P, Q, and R.

**Solution:**

Express all shares in terms of Q: P = 5Q, R = 5Q/3

Total = P + Q + R = 5Q + Q + 5Q/3 = 12,029

Solving the above equation we get Q = Rs. 1569

Therefore, R's share = 5Q/3 = 5 × 1569/3 = Rs. 2615

**Therefore, the share of R is Rs. 2615.**

questions.question: Sum of the angles made by a chord at the centre and on the major arc of a circle is 225 degree. What will be the angle made at the major arc of this circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **angle subtended by a chord at the centre** is always **twice** the angle subtended by it on the **major arc**.

Ratio of **Angle at Centre** : **Angle on Major Arc** = 2 : 1

Total Ratio Units = 2 + 1 = 3 units

Given: 3 units = 225°

1 unit = 225° ÷ 3 = 75°

**∴ The correct answer is 75 degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of **angle at the centre** and **angle on the major arc** = 225°.

**Formula Used:**

Angle subtended by an **arc** at the **centre** is **double** the angle subtended by it at any point on the **remaining part** of the circle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca177ea910ffc214ff95531146fdf7b9fb312e07664414406ce7b254e4277138.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the angle subtended by the chord at the **major arc** be x.

⇒ Angle subtended at the **centre** = 2x

⇒ x + 2x = 225°

⇒ 3x = 225°

⇒ x = 225° ÷ 3

⇒ x = 75°

**∴ The correct answer is 75 degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inscribed Angle Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is exactly twice the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the circle's circumference (major arc).

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same chord or arc at different points on the same segment (major or minor) of the circle are always equal.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The sum of the angle at the major arc and the angle at the minor arc subtended by the same chord is 180°, as they form opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral.</p

questions.question: The average runs scored by a batsman in 7 matches is 49 and in other 9 matches the average is 27. What is the average runs scored by the batsman in these 16 matches?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Average runs in 7 matches = 49

Average runs in 9 matches = 27

**Concept:**

The total average is the sum of all runs divided by the total number of matches.

**Solution:**

Total runs in 7 matches = 7 × 49 = 343

Total runs in 9 matches = 9 × 27 = 243

Total runs in 16 matches = 343 + 243 = 586

Average runs in 16 matches = 586/16 = 36.625

**Therefore, the average runs scored by the batsman in these 16 matches is 36.625.**
